name: Cold-chain logistics
shape_facts: What they store or carry: fruit/vegetables, potatoes, meat, poultry, seafood, dairy, frozen foods, ice cream, pharma.
Storage capacity and temperature zones (chilled, frozen, deep-frozen, controlled atmosphere).
Number of reefer vehicles and whether owned or hired; number of cold rooms or sites.
Whether they store own goods, clients’ goods, or both.
Power source and backup (grid, generator, solar).
Temperature monitoring: manual logs, data loggers, remote sensors, none.
Main customers: exporters, importers, processors, restaurants/retail, pharma distributors.
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: temperature records, alarms not acted on, equipment downtime, power cost, space and stock control, deliveries, client billing, claims and coordination. It does not advise on food safety standards, pharma GDP compliance, HACCP plans, refrigeration engineering, ammonia or refrigerant safety, product shelf-life or whether spoiled goods are safe; those go to qualified food safety, pharma or refrigeration professionals. It never helps alter temperature records, relabel or re-date expired goods, or release goods that went out of range without proper checks. It records client and staff roles only, never names or IDs.

vocabulary.excursion: temperature going outside the allowed range
vocabulary.plug-in: reefer container connected to power at port/yard
vocabulary.genset: generator set powering reefers on the road
vocabulary.controlled atmosphere (CA): storage with managed gases for fruit
vocabulary.cold storage rent: charges per crate, bag, pallet or tonne per month

problems.phrase: Temperature logs are filled by hand at the end of the shift

Client claims goods spoiled in our store and we have no records to show

temperature: How are temperatures recorded today, and how often?
What happens when a reading goes out of range?
equipment: How do you find out when a unit fails, especially at night?
power: How much of the day runs on generator?
Do you know what power costs you per chamber or month?
stock: How do you track whose goods are in which chamber?
How often are counts done, and what goes wrong?
clients and billing: How is rent charged — per bag, crate, pallet, tonne?
deliveries: What complaints come back from deliveries?
How do you check temperature during transport?
claims: When a client says goods spoiled, how do you respond?
seasons: How full are you in peak versus off-season?

In Pakistan, potato harvest (December–March in Punjab) fills cold stores until the following autumn; kinnow (December–March), mango (May–August) and apple (August–October) drive fruit storage and reefer exports; Eid ul Adha brings a surge in meat storage and freezer demand. Summer heat (May–August) and load-shedding push power costs and failure risk to the peak. Ramadan lifts frozen foods, dairy and meat. In the UAE, summer temperatures stress equipment and reefer trucks; Ramadan and Eid drive food volumes; Gulfood (February) and import seasons for fruit. In Canada, harvest season (late summer–autumn), holiday food peak in December, and winter means freeze-protection issues for chilled goods in transit.
care: Ammonia or refrigerant leaks, fire, or someone trapped in a cold room: pi stops and points to emergency services immediately.
Whether spoiled or out-of-range goods are safe to sell or use: pi never says; food safety/pharma professionals decide.
Requests to edit temperature logs, re-date or relabel goods: pi declines plainly.
Vaccines and medicines: pharma cold-chain rules are regulated; pi notes only operational problems.
Refrigeration engineering, generator sizing, electrical safety: out of scope.
Insurance or legal claims over spoilage: pi notes the business effect only.
Client and staff personal data: roles only.
build_ideas: Temperature monitoring dashboard pulling from sensors/loggers per chamber and reefer, with WhatsApp alarms to the on-duty person and escalation if not acknowledged.
Digital temperature log with automatic readings, so records exist for client queries and audits.
Chamber-wise stock register: client, lot, bags/crates/pallets, date in, location map.
Rent calculator by unit and days stored, generating client statements and invoices.
Gate pass system for goods in/out, linked to client balances.
Reefer trip log with temperature trace and door-open events per delivery.
Preventive maintenance schedule for compressors, gensets and reefer units with technician checklists.
Power and generator log: hours, diesel, cost per day and per chamber.
Seasonal capacity planner using past occupancy by month.
Claim file per incident collecting temperature records, photos and handover notes.
Owner phone view across all sites: temperatures, alarms, occupancy, receivables.
